beats.care: If you plan a UK degree, an offer letter is no longer a sure thing. Confirm it before paying any non-refundable fees.
beats.what: Some UK universities are withdrawing admission offers to international students, including Indians, to avoid breaking tougher Home Office visa rules.
beats.why: Since June, a university risks losing its licence if more than 5% of its offer-holders are refused visas, down from 10%.

cards.note: Financial Times analysis of Home Office data, via Business Standard
cards.title: Share of UK study visa applications withdrawn, first half of 2026

cards.body: Universities are also graded on enrolment (at least 95%) and course completion (at least 90%). Their rating is set by their weakest number, so one bad figure can cost them the right to recruit abroad.
cards.title: why would a uni cancel my offer?

cards.body: London's Bloomsbury Institute lost its licence to sponsor international students after failing the checks. Sunderland paused applications from some African countries for January 2027.
Some experts think the squeeze could push UK universities to recruit more from India and China, where refusal rates are lower.

cards.q: Is the UK still worth it?

opts: Too many visa refusals can cost them their licence
cards.q: Why are some UK universities pulling offers?
cards.why: The stricter 5% refusal cap means universities play safe by admitting fewer students they see as risky.
